original_test_intent: Verify BF3 Port 1 physical LED color and cadence for connected, disconnected, I/O-active and owner-commanded states.
original_method: A qualified on-site operator confirms the exact Port 1 cage and link partner, performs only an approved cable-state and I/O/command sequence, records synchronized link telemetry and visual evidence, and restores the production-safe link state.
manual_activity: An on-site operator labels BF3 Port 1 and its peer, follows the approved connect/disconnect, I/O and amber-command matrix, captures each LED state on video, then verifies link restoration.
required_inputs: Exact BF3 device serial/PCI identity, front-panel Port 1 cage and peer endpoint
Cable type/part, port ownership, redundancy and approved live versus powered-down handling state
Whether green and amber are separate emitters, a bicolor package or mutually exclusive modes
Expected color combination for link-up/link-down and negotiation/training states
Approved bounded I/O stimulus, expected green-blink cadence/duty and observation time
Reviewed command/interface for Amber Blink, allowed target, effects, duration and cleanup
Passive link state/speed/width/error counters and event sources
Camera/color/timing evidence standard plus independent network/fabric/platform recovery
safety_requirements: Verify Port 1 and peer identity at both ends before cable action
Confirm redundancy and workload impact; do not disconnect an active sole production path
Do not invent the Amber Blink command or use Port 2 controls as a substitute
Use a bounded approved I/O stimulus and do not infer LED color from link telemetry
Stop on failed link recovery, unexpected errors, thermal/power fault, wrong-port indication or unsafe access
Restore and independently verify the original cable routing, link parameters and service health
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact Port 1 topology, approved cable state, stimulus and recovery plan
Collect passive pre/post link identity, negotiation, counters and event context
Organize synchronized operator photo/video for each visual state
Check evidence completeness and restoration without interpreting color as an automated verdict
Perform no cable handling, traffic generation, LED command, reset, power action, automatic retry or PASS/FAIL decision
engineer_actions: Approve Port 1/peer/cable identity and safe disconnect window
Define LED element semantics and connected/disconnected combinations
Approve bounded I/O stimulus and exact amber-blink command with cleanup
Review visual/link evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly non-runnable for acceptance because direct color/cadence and cable state need human observation; the amber command and safe stimuli are absent.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use an owner-approved manual matrix with synchronized video and passive link telemetry; any stimulus command remains separately reviewed and operator-controlled.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BF3 Port 1, connected/disconnected plus green/amber solid/blink states and 15/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL PORT1 LED REVIEW REQUIRES LINK-IMPACT PLAN AND REVIEWED AMBER COMMAND
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture the labeled local and peer ports, cable state, link telemetry and LED video on a common timeline for each approved transition, then verify negotiation and counters after reconnection.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact port/peer identity, impact control, cadence measurement and objective link restoration evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Port 2 is an independent lane/cage/path; identical behavior wording does not make its observation reusable.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A cable can be inserted while link training repeatedly fails, producing activity-like blinking. Visual evidence must be correlated with stable link-up parameters and error counters before an engineer interprets it.

project_override_considerations: If green and amber are two simultaneous LEDs, the owner must define valid combinations; if they are a bicolor element, mutually exclusive color behavior must be stated. The source wording alone cannot decide this topology.
expected_evidence: Approved BF3 device, Port 1 cage, cable and peer mapping plus impact/redundancy plan
LED element semantics and state/stimulus/cadence matrix including reviewed amber command
Timestamped context and close video for connected, disconnected, I/O and command cases
Synchronized pre/post link state, negotiated parameters, counters, events and service recovery

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Green Solid and Amber Solid share connected/disconnected wording but may represent two emitters or valid combined behavior; the source is ambiguous and incomplete, not conclusively contradictory without the LED topology.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Port 1 visual intent is identifiable and manually executable after owner approval of topology, cable impact, stimuli and recovery.

review_improvement: Adds port/peer identity, redundancy gating, LED-element semantics, measurable cadence and link-restoration proof specific to Port 1.
independent_technical_reasoning: Physical link presence does not prove a healthy BF3 data path: repeated training or error recovery can toggle an activity indicator while traffic fails. A valid Port 1 observation must pair the LED timeline with stable negotiated link parameters and counters, and must not borrow a visually similar response from Port 2.
